sectionsContent.title: Intermolecular Forces
sectionsContent.conceptLabel: OPTIONAL — WORTH 1 POINT ON YOUR UNIT 5 TEST

concept.summary: Complete this and turn it in at test time to add 1 point to your Unit 5 test score. Polarity decides the IMFs.
keyIdeas: Hydrogen bonding: H on N, O, or F pulled to another N, O, or F. Strongest of the three IMFs.
London dispersion: every molecule. The only IMF in nonpolar ones.

sectionsContent.directions: Part A: each polar bond already has a dipole arrow pointing toward the δ− atom. Use the arrows and the shape to decide polar or nonpolar, then circle every IMF the molecule has. Part B: draw the shape and add a dipole arrow beside each polar bond (cross at the δ+ end), then do the same. London dispersion is in every molecule, so circle it every time. EN: H 2.20 · C 2.55 · F 3.98 · Si 1.90 · S 2.58 · Cl 3.16.

blocks.label: PART B · YOU DRAW IT (shape + dipole arrows)
blocks.heading: Intermolecular Forces · Part B

keyNotes: 1 point per row, 10 total. The point needs the right polarity and exactly the right IMFs circled. London dispersion is circled on every row.
Hydrogen bonding needs H bonded to N, O or F: CH₃OH (O–H), CH₃NH₂ (N–H), HF. CH₃Cl and CH₃F are the traps: they have H, but the H is on C, so dipole–dipole + London dispersion only.
CF₄ and SiCl₄: polar bonds (1.43 and 1.26) in a symmetric tetrahedron cancel, so nonpolar. CF₄ vs CH₃F: same shape, but one different atom makes CH₃F polar.
I₂: no polar bonds at all, London dispersion only. Slide 35: more electrons, stronger LDF, so I₂ is a solid.
HF: ΔEN 3.98 − 2.20 = 1.78, polar covalent, just under 1.80 (same call as the 4.5 sheet).
SF₂: S has 2 bonds and 2 lone pairs, so bent like OF₂ and H₂O; the pulls do not cancel. S–F 1.40.

Drawings follow the 5.4 sheet: outer lone pairs may be left off; an arrow on each polar bond (C–H 0.35 gets none); polar molecules get a long net arrow, nonpolar ones net = 0. Accept any clear arrow placement that points the right way.
